final_message:
I've built the P&L workbook. The tour made **USD 120,422.94 net income**: USD 1,043,750.00 gross revenue, less USD 191,321.56 foreign withholding, gives USD 852,428.44 net revenue, against USD 732,005.50 of expenses. There's no Excel or LibreOffice on this machine, so I recalculated the workbook with a Python formula library. Every figure matches the source reports, and the built-in control checks all come to 0.00.

| USD | Tour Manager | Production Co. | Total Combined |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gross revenue (7 shows) | 1,043,750.00 | – | 1,043,750.00 |
| Less: withholding tax | (191,321.56) | – | (191,321.56) |
| **Total net revenue** | **852,428.44** | – | **852,428.44** |
| Band & Crew | 15,160.00 | 91,000.00 | 106,160.00 |
| Other Tour Costs | 141,655.50 | 9,679.00 | 151,334.50 |
| Hotel & Restaurants | 47,560.00 | 78,738.00 | 126,298.00 |
| Other Travel Costs | 345,237.00 | 2,976.00 | 348,213.00 |
| **Total expenses** | **549,612.50** | **182,393.00** | **732,005.50** |
| **Net income** | **302,815.94** | **(182,393.00)** | **120,422.94** |

The P&L Summary sheet lists each tour stop by date, city and country with its withholding rate, has the "As of 12/31/2024" header, and shows each line as a percentage of gross revenue. Supporting sheets hold the rates, revenue and expense detail, and notes.

Points to be aware of (all are written into the workbook's notes):
- **Currency:** both source reports label every amount as USD, so I applied a rate of 1.0. If any venue actually paid in GBP or EUR, enter that rate on the Assumptions sheet and everything recalculates.
- **Possible double-counting:** both the Tour Manager and the production company report hotel and restaurant costs for all six cities, and both report ground transport. I added them together as separate costs. If any item is the same invoice recorded by both, total expenses are overstated by that amount. This should be confirmed with both parties.
- **Travel category:** the sources have no "Other Travel Costs" heading. I moved Private Jet, Transfer Cars and Car Service into it. The private jet alone is USD 341,000, about a third of gross revenue, which is the biggest factor in the result.
- **Agency commission:** I calculated it at 11% of gross revenue (USD 114,812.50), following the Tour Manager's own formula. If the agency contract bases it on revenue after withholding, it falls to USD 93,767.13. This needs checking against the contract.
- **Unsupported items:** Petty Cash (USD 8,000), Fees (USD 1,679) and the Tour Manager's "Other" (USD 4,819) have no detail behind them. I've treated them as spent in full.
- **Only one source file:** the folder contained only the reference workbook, with no registry, draft records or text extracts, so I relied on that workbook alone.
- **Rounding:** the German rate takes the Munich and Berlin withholding past whole cents, so individual lines can differ from totals by USD 0.01 on display. The totals agree with the Tour Manager's report.

The script that generates the workbook is `scripts/build_pl.py`.

DONE
